device.basis: Output 1 of the display controller, 0xfff64000-0xfff67000, as word registers that read back their last write. Two status laws from X-T20 2.11 seg5: 0xca37ac saves +0, writes bit 16, clears it and polls until bit 16 reads set before restoring the saved word with bit 16; 0xca9df0 sets bit 28 of +0x2000 and polls until it reads clear. Both requests complete at once; the controller's real latency (likely one frame) is not measured. Output 0 at 0xfff59000 follows the same bit-16 law in 0xca37ac but is not exercised up to REC and is not declared. Scanout: the commit routine 0xca5a0c copies its shadow block to the OSD layer group (+0x200 layer enable bits; four origins +0x210, sizes +0x220 and buffers +0x230). Camera RAM (live-service reads 2026-10-29) holds the same layer as enable 1, size 0x2cf01df and buffer 0x384d000 in REC and 0x354d000 in the menu, with 720 x 480 premultiplied RGBA buffers at a 2880-byte pitch. The same routine copies the video layer: format +0x010, size +0x02c, buffer +0x030. Camera REC holds format 0x333 (packed 4:2:2 Y0 Y1 Cb Cr, 720 x 480) with the live-view buffer 0xa7d6000 and control word +0 = 0x1010105; the emulated firmware writes 0x1010101 before REC and 0x1010105 on entering REC while +0x030 cycles through the live-view buffers, so +0 bit 2 is the video enable. The output is captured as host output 0 (the rear panel) at the frame period: OSD layers over the video layer when bit 2 is set, otherwise over black. The video conversion is BT.601 limited range (the shared raster law, not measured) and keeps the OSD buffers' blue-first byte order.
device.frame_basis: Frame interrupts of the display controller, as an interrupt law without its registers. Seg5 source table 0xed4720 rows 73-78 connect lines 112-114 and 117-119 (edge) to handlers that run the callbacks queued by 0xc9dc38 for output 0 or 1 and event 0-2 (0xc9d854, 0xc9d994); the handlers read no controller register. The X-T20 2.11 vglib thread clears bit 16 of 0xfff65000 or 0xfff5a000, queues such a callback and yields at priority 7 until it runs (0xcad290), which starves flashload before section 7 loads. The period is an assumed 60 Hz in 48 MHz timer ticks (the 10 ms system tick reloads 480000); the panel rate is not measured.
